branch_hypotheses.observable_divergence_signal: Riverbend adopts a resolution, notice, or budget action inconsistent with continued compact participation.
branch_hypotheses.plausible_alternate_path: Conflict shifts from bargaining to implementation breakdown and public blame assignment.

branch_hypotheses.observable_divergence_signal: Formal legal memo, filing, or injunction-related action enters the public record.

branch_hypotheses.plausible_alternate_path: Economic arguments reduce the appeal of hard exit and increase support for a limited compromise.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Preservation can coexist with unresolved conflict or a temporary compromise; it is contradicted by formal exit or durable suspension.
endpoint_ledger.description: The regional compact remains operative with all three towns participating at least minimally.
endpoint_ledger.label: Compact preserved

meta.important_question: Does the three-town compact remain intact, or does a member town successfully exit or suspend participation?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Compact continuity is the central institutional stake and precondition for several coordinated solutions.
realization_criteria: No town has formally exited or suspended participation by the close of the observed horizon.
Regional compact board continues recognized coordination activity with all three towns represented.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: T0 includes a withdrawal threat but no realized exit.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Temporary intake coordination without formal launch does not satisfy this endpoint.
endpoint_ledger.description: A regional shared intake center moves from proposal to formal authorization and operational launch.
endpoint_ledger.label: Shared intake center implemented

meta.important_question: Is a shared regional intake center formally authorized and implemented beyond proposal status?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: The intake center is a focal mechanism but not yet a realized terminal outcome.
realization_criteria: At least two required governing authorities formally approve the shared intake arrangement.
An operational start date, site, or service launch for the intake center is publicly established.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Only a proposal exists at initialization.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: A symbolic pause or temporary rhetoric shift without defined allocation terms does not qualify.
endpoint_ledger.description: The towns reach an observable agreement on funding, quotas, service responsibilities, or cost distribution sufficient to stabilize cooperation.
endpoint_ledger.label: Negotiated burden-sharing deal

meta.important_question: Do the towns reach a negotiated burden-sharing or shared funding arrangement acceptable enough to reduce acute coalition fracture?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Burden-sharing is the main merge path that could resolve or soften multiple conflicts at once.
realization_criteria: A written or publicly announced inter-town agreement defines cost-sharing or responsibility allocation.
At least two towns and the regional compact board affirm implementation of the agreed terms.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Negotiation pressure is strong but no settlement is yet recorded.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Informal legal advice alone is insufficient; observable formal escalation is required.
endpoint_ledger.description: The compact dispute enters a formal legal phase over authority to withdraw, funding duties, or enforcement.
endpoint_ledger.label: Formal legal challenge

meta.important_question: Does the dispute shift into a formal legal challenge over withdrawal rights or funding obligations?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Legal escalation is a distinct terminal pathway if politics cannot contain the withdrawal dispute.
realization_criteria: A formal legal filing, injunction request, or equivalent public legal action is initiated.
Compact counsel or a court becomes part of the active dispute record beyond advisory review.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Legal challenge is an explicit scenario path but remains unrealized at T0.

causal_premises: Regional migration inflow increases demand for shelter and intake coordination.
Shelter strain creates conflict over cost-sharing and intake responsibilities.
Labor demand from employers creates incentives for accommodation rather than exclusion.
Charity overload reduces buffer capacity and raises urgency for formal coordination.
Threatened unilateral withdrawal increases coalition fracture risk and may trigger legal or political contestation.
simulation_brief.summary: A regional migration surge is straining shelter capacity across three towns. One town proposes a shared intake center, another threatens to withdraw from an existing compact, employers need workers, and charities are overloaded. Core pressures involve intergovernmental authority, shared funding, unilateral exit, possible legal challenge, and negotiated burden-sharing.
uncertainties: Exact legal structure of the inter-town compact is unspecified.
Population magnitudes and shelter capacity are not provided.
Decision rules for funding and exit are implied but not fully described.
No named towns or organizations are provided; actors are fictionalized placeholders.

sociology_baseline.note: Residents likely respond more to proposals close to prior fairness beliefs than to maximal positions.
Many residents remain passive unless visible service disruption or elite conflict intensifies.
Affected newcomers have high private stakes but low public expression due to vulnerability.
Town-level publics likely cluster around local identity and fairness narratives.
Policy shifts are more likely after reinforcement from multiple institutions such as charities, employers, and a second town.
Local town identity shapes attitudes toward burden-sharing and exit threats.
Attention may fade if no acute visible trigger occurs, but current strain keeps baseline attention moderate.

sociology_prompt_influences.effect: Raises sensitivity to perceived unequal burden distribution.
Visible charity overload increases openness to coordination mechanisms.
Workforce demand supports pragmatic accommodation and intake stabilization.
Threatened withdrawal elevates coalition fracture as a focal concern.
Unclear withdrawal authority increases procedural caution and legal maneuvering.
